title: eval-harness: add CI hook for prompt-set regression + quality gating integration
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR introduces a CI hook and integration points for prompt-set regression checks and quality gating into the eval-harness pipeline. Motivation: teams have been seeing silent regressions when prompt sets are edited or added without running the eval suite; current gating is manual and inconsistent. This change implements an automatic CI step that: 1) detects modified prompt sets and runs the eval-harness against a small, fast set of baseline metrics (latency, token-quality, top-k accuracy for rerank tasks, semantic-similarity thresholds for paraphrase prompts); 2) computes a compact metrics diff compared to the preserved baseline for the target model(s); 3) applies a configurable quality gate (thresholds are stored in eval-harness/config/quality_gates.toml) and fails CI when regressions exceed defined tolerances; 4) produces an artifacts zip with detailed eval results and a short human-readable summary to be posted on the PR. Implementation notes: - added ci/workflows/eval-harness-gate.yml which is triggered on PRs that touch eval-harness/prompts/** and relevant code paths; the workflow uses a lightweight runner with cached model variants for speed. - added eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py which handles prompt diffing, scheduling targeted eval jobs, aggregation, and summary generation. - added a small pytest suite eval-harness/tests/test_prompt_gating.py covering the gating logic and parsing of metrics. - documentation: docs/eval/quality-gating.md explains the gate semantics and how to configure thresholds per-model. Backwards compatibility and opt-out: the hook is opt-in by default (project-level flag in .github/eval-gate-config.yml) to avoid surprising existing workflows; org-admins can enable at repo-level via a repo setting. Checklist: [x] design doc reviewed, [x] unit tests added, [x] CI workflow validated on a staging runner, [x] docs added, [x] feature flagged for gradual rollout. Testing performed: ran the hook against a representative set of prompt diffs (add, modify, remove), validated that small non-actionable metric noise (<0.5% on primary metric) does not fail, and that a simulated regression (2-3% drop on top-k accuracy) triggers a failing gate and attaches the artifacts. Risk and mitigation: the main risk is CI time; mitigated by targeted eval selection, model caching, and an execution timeout with fallback to a warning mode if the workflow times out. Follow-ups: integrate gating results into the Redwood Console alerts and add a per-team baseline management UI (ENG-2199).
